comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C43-C46 regarding the histone reporter system. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites specific figure data while peer reviewers praise the 'very high quality' microscopy and describe the reporters as 'a powerful tool.'

Perfect agreement on claims C2, C3, C38, C53, C54, C56 regarding H3.1 eviction and nuclear changes in infected cells. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with strong quantitative data. Peer reviewers confirm the findings and praise the 'compelling imaging-based approaches.'

Strong agreement on claims C4, C39, C58 regarding G2 arrest in infected cells. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C67, C68 which peer review addresses separately in R5. Both confirm cells remain in G2 without progressing to M phase.

Strong agreement on claims C40, C59, C60, C75 regarding tetraploidy and 8C DNA content. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review R4 also addresses C61-C63 (covered by OpenEval R8), confirming endomitotic tetraploid state in nodule primordium cells.

Partial overlap on claims C41, C55 regarding cell cycle exit characteristics. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 groups these with C57, C74 as part of broader interpretation about cell state, while peer R3 focuses on G2 arrest markers.

Minimal overlap on claim C74 regarding cell-cycle control and infection competence. Both evaluations find the overall interpretation SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 treats this as part of the cell state characterization, while peer R7 emphasizes the dual role concept.

Agreement on claims C5, C42, C66, C69 regarding NF-YA1's role in G2/M regulation, but with different confidence levels. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate cautious language, while peer review rates it UNCERTAIN, noting 'definitive proof needs more investigation' and using 'likely' qualifier.

Minimal overlap on claims C67, C68 regarding G2/M markers. OpenEval R3 finds evidence SUPPORTED as part of G2 arrest demonstration, while peer R5 groups these with NF-YA1 mechanism claims and expresses more uncertainty about the regulatory mechanism.

Agreement on claim C73 regarding NF-YA1's dual role in cell division and infection. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites specific data from Figure 9, while peer review accepts the dual role concept without expressing concerns.

Agreement on claims C61-C63 regarding maintained tetraploidy and nodule fitness. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval R8 treats these separately from C40, C59, C60, C75, while peer R4 groups all ploidy-related claims together.

Perfect agreement on claim C76 regarding the hypothetical transcriptional landscape. Both evaluations rate this UNCERTAIN, recognizing it as speculation beyond direct experimental evidence. Both note the cell state characterization is supported but the broader hypothesis requires validation.

Minimal overlap on claim C52 regarding H3.1/H3.3 dynamics in arbuscular mycorrhiza symbiosis. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval R10 groups this with C47-C51 as background/validation claims, while peer R6 treats it as an important confirmation of previous findings.
